from: From: IT Services, to all staff
title: A security incident
body: Someone has been reading the company's records from a car park in another country. IT Services stresses that no customer data was affected, and then, an hour later, that some was. Everyone is to change their password to something they will remember, and not to write it down.
changed: The breach put the Senior Analyst in charge of the review, which gave them a say in everything.

story.reported: The company's security posture was validated by a real-world exercise.
story.happened: Someone read everything from a car park, and nobody can say for how long.

from: From: Hugh Lamb, Head of Operations
title: Simplifying how we work
body: Following a review, some reporting lines are being simplified, so the Senior Analyst now reports directly to your boss's boss, which simplifies things for the Senior Analyst, while your boss remains your boss. A new chart is available, and the old chart has been recalled.
changed: A reorganisation moved the Senior Analyst out from under your boss, and up.

clue.text: Someone has left a draft org chart on the photocopier, with arrows on it in pencil.

story.reported: The organisation was simplified, and is now more agile.
story.happened: The chart changed, and nothing else did, except who you can complain to.

from: From: The Board, to all staff
title: An exciting approach
body: A company nobody has heard of has made an offer for the company. The Board wishes to reassure everyone that nothing will change, and that everyone should update their CVs for an unrelated reason. The Project Co-ordinator has been moved under your boss's boss, to help with the numbers.
changed: The takeover bid sent the Project Co-ordinator upstairs to help with the numbers, and took your boss down a peg.

clue.text: Two people in very good suits were in the lift, counting the floors and writing them down.

story.reported: The company attracted significant external interest, which is a tribute to its people.
story.happened: Someone tried to buy the company, and looked at the floor you work on, and laughed.

from: From: Hugh Lamb, Head of Operations
title: A secondment
body: Special Projects has asked for someone with a proven record of being available, and your boss has been seconded to it, upstairs, with immediate effect and a larger chair. Your boss says that it is a great honour, and that it came as a complete surprise, and has already measured the chair.
changed: A secondment moved your boss up to Special Projects, and left their seat open.

clue.text: Your boss got out of the lift on the wrong floor, the one above, and stayed there for an hour.

story.reported: The floor's leadership was recognised with an opportunity to lead elsewhere.
story.happened: Your boss went upstairs, and the seat stayed downstairs, empty, with everyone looking at it.

from: From: Hugh Lamb, Head of Operations
title: A new post
body: Following a review of spans and layers, a new post is being created to lead your team, so that your boss can focus on leading it. Your boss keeps the title, the office and the plant. The new post gets the team. A chart is attached, and it has a box on it with nobody in it.
changed: A restructure created a post to lead your boss's team, and your boss kept the title.

clue.text: Someone has left a chart on the photocopier with an empty box on it, just above your name.

story.reported: The organisation added leadership capacity at the front line.
story.happened: A post was invented to do your boss's job, and your boss was asked to support it.

title: A secondment to Floor 3
body: Floor 3 has asked for someone who knows how operations really work, and your boss has been seconded there, with immediate effect, to explain it. Your boss says that it is a stretch opportunity, and has already stretched, in the direction of the lift.
changed: A secondment moved your boss up to Floor 3, and left their seat open.

clue.text: Your boss has started taking the lift up to Floor 3 for coffee, which is free there, and staying for lunch, which is not.

story.reported: Operational leadership was deployed where it could add most value.
story.happened: Your boss went upstairs to add value, and left the seat downstairs, with its value still in it.

from: From: Simone Fairley, Head of Transformation
title: A new post at the top of Floor 3
body: Following a review of spans and layers, a post of Programme Director is being created to lead your boss's portfolio, so that your boss can focus on leading it. Your boss keeps the title and the view. The new post gets the portfolio, and a chart with a box on it at the top of Floor 3, with nobody in it.
changed: A restructure created a post at the top of Floor 3, to lead your boss's portfolio, and your boss kept the title.

clue.text: Someone has left a chart in the scanner with a box at the top of Floor 3, and no name in it.

story.reported: Floor 3 strengthened its leadership of the portfolio.
story.happened: A post was invented above your boss to do your boss's job, and your boss was asked to welcome it.

title: Water in the server room
body: A pipe that was not on any plan has emptied itself into the server room. Nobody could have known about it, and Facilities has a form saying so. Everything since Tuesday has gone, including, by coincidence, the good things.

story.reported: The company completed an unscheduled review of its data.
story.happened: A pipe burst and took everyone's work with it, and for once it was nobody's fault.

from: From: The Board, to all staff
title: A leadership transition
body: You learn from the news that the Chief Executive has left, to spend more time with a yacht. An interim has been appointed, and has asked the Office Co-ordinator to report to your boss, for reasons the interim has not been in the building long enough to explain.
changed: A new interim Chief Executive moved the Office Co-ordinator under your boss, for no reason anyone could give.

story.reported: The company welcomed a new phase of leadership.
story.happened: The Chief Executive left in a hurry, and since nobody on your floor had ever met them, it changed nothing, and everything.

title: Please do not delete anything
body: A regulator has written about something that happened before any of you worked here. Nobody may delete anything until further notice. Everybody has now thought of something they wish they had deleted last week.

story.reported: The company is working openly with its regulators.
story.happened: A letter arrived about something older than everyone, and everyone looked guilty anyway.
